title: AB Means B First, Then A
topic: Matrix multiplication is function composition. Applying B then A gives AB. Order matters: AB ≠ BA in general.

beats.narration: Two transformations, two orders. Does it matter which one you do first?
Take matrix A — a rotation by forty-five degrees. And matrix B — a stretch along x, a squeeze along y.

elements.content: Standard grid with unit square highlighted

beats.narration: Apply B first — the unit square stretches and squashes. Then apply A — the deformed square rotates. The single matrix A B captures both steps at once.

elements.content: Unit square morphs from identity → B (stretched parallelogram)
Then morphs from B → BA-applied (rotated stretched parallelogram)
AB matrix appears alongside, highlighting it equals the same final result

beats.narration: Now swap the order. Apply A first, then B. The square rotates, then stretches — and lands somewhere different. The matrix B A is not the same as A B.

elements.content: Left pane: AB result (parallelogram from previous beat) shown faded
Right pane: A then B sequence — unit square rotates then stretches, ending in different shape
Side-by-side comparison: AB vs BA, both parallelograms shown together

beats.narration: A B means B first, then A — A acts last on whatever B produced. And in general, A B does not equal B A.

elements.content: AB acts right-to-left: B first, then A.
AB ≠ BA in general — order is part of the operation.
